title: AI-Assisted Classification under Correlation Neglect and Trust
claim: Regions where assistance helps, hurts, or is replaced by automation shift with the human's trust level, so the best trust depends on deployment.
layout: 3 panels side-by-side, left-to-right, shared axes with dotted threshold reference lines
description: Three side-by-side phase diagrams, captioned (a) Undertrust, (b) Calibrated, (c) Overtrust, with trust parameter beta-hat of 0.5, 1 and 1.5. Each has AI capability tau_A on the horizontal axis and overlap lambda on the vertical axis. The plane is shaded in three regions: pink for complementarity (Comp.), gray for impairment (Imp.) at the top left, and lavender for automation (Auto.) on the right. A red solid line rises to a black dot at tau_H, a blue solid curve falls away from it, and a dashed black curve marks the feasibility boundary. Red and blue dotted reference lines mark threshold values (0.60, 0.80, 0.87 and 1.41, 1.62, 1.72). The gray impairment region grows from left to right across panels. The eye goes first to the colored regions and the red-blue boundary curves.
caption: Phase diagrams under correlation neglect (ˆα = 0) for three trust regimes. The deployment space (τA, λ) is partitioned into complementarity (HA optimal, red), impairment (H optimal, gray), and automation (AI optimal, blue). The dashed black curve marks the cue-pool feasibility boundary τA = τH/λ. The augmentation threshold becomes positive at λ > 1 −ˆβ/2 (vertical-axis tick): 0.75, 0.50, 0.25 across panels (a)–(c), so the impairment region becomes active at lower overlap as trust rises. Dotted reference lines mark threshold values at fixed λ: at λ = 0.9 (red), the augmentation threshold τaug shifts from 0.60 to 0.80 to 0.87, and at λ = 0.5 (blue), the automation threshold τauto shifts from 1.41 to 1.62 to 1.72.
abstract: When does an AI assistant improve human decision-making, and when does it hurt? We argue that the answer depends not just on AI accuracy but also on how much its evidence overlaps with the human's and how the human combines the two. A worker makes a binary decision by observing her own signal and receiving a recommendation from an AI. We develop a human behavioral model with two primitives: her awareness of the overlap and her trust in the AI. Our analysis gives a closed-form phase diagram over AI capability and overlap, with regions of complementarity, impairment, and automation. A worker who neglects the overlap (correlation neglect) can be made less accurate by a more capable AI, double-counting the shared evidence. Trust reshapes the regions - undertrust may compensate for correlation neglect, so that the trust level maximizing accuracy depends on the deployment parameters. Empirically, we identify the two model parameters by pairing the same workers with different AIs, and break the accuracy loss into a correlation-neglect cost and an undertrust cost, one tied to reducing overlap on the AI side, the other to calibrating trust on the human side. On ChatBench, AI assistance raises accuracy by 21 points, yet workers apply only about a quarter of the Bayes-rational weight to AI information; GPT-4o falls in the automation region and Llama-3.1-8b stays at the complementarity boundary; and calibrating trust recovers about 2.6 points for GPT-4o but almost nothing for Llama-3.1-8b.
